datasets.title: Italy: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/ita-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

lineage.description: FAPAR values from VIIRS satellite observations are collected in 10-day composites and processed by JRC to calculate anomalies as deviations from a long-term mean baseline (2012 to present). The resulting raster datasets are distributed as annual GeoTIFF files to enable detection and monitoring of agricultural drought impacts on vegetation growth and productivity across Italy.

sources.name: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.description: Provides VIIRS-derived FAPAR satellite observations processed into 10-day composites with anomaly calculations relative to 2012-present baseline for drought monitoring

sources.name: Copernicus
sources.description: Copernicus Earth observation program providing the satellite data infrastructure and processing framework for vegetation monitoring
